books.title: Physics Part I
books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (First Edition December 2006; Revised Edition November 2022; reprinted February 2026)

books.title: Physics Part II
books.edition: Revised Edition November 2022, reprinted December 2025 (First Edition March 2007); chapter PDFs 9-13 are footed "Reprint 2026-27", chapter 14 is footed "Reprint 2025-26", the prelims carry no reprint footer

source.method: chapter titles from each book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings (Introduction, Summary, Points to Ponder and Exercises are not topics; a parent heading that is only a lead-in to its subsections is merged with them; short subsections are grouped under their section heading)

topics.title: Electric Charge
objectives: Student can state that there are two kinds of charge, positive and negative, and that like charges repel and unlike charges attract
Student can explain why a glass rod rubbed with silk and the silk acquire opposite charges
Student can describe how a gold-leaf electroscope detects charge on a body
visualIdeas: two glass rods repelling and a glass rod attracting a plastic rod
gold-leaf electroscope with leaves diverging

topics.title: Conductors and Insulators
objectives: Student can distinguish conductors, which allow charge to move through them, from insulators, which do not
Student can explain why charge given to a conductor spreads over its whole surface while charge on an insulator stays where it is put
Student can explain why a metal rod held in the hand does not show charging but a plastic comb does
visualIdeas: charge spreading over a metal sphere vs staying in a patch on a plastic rod

topics.title: Basic Properties of Electric Charge
objectives: Student can treat small charged bodies as point charges
Student can state that charges add algebraically (additivity) and that the total charge of an isolated system is conserved
Student can explain quantisation of charge, q = ne, and calculate the number of electrons in a given charge
visualIdeas: number line adding +q and -q charges
electrons transferring from one body to another during rubbing

topics.title: Coulomb's Law
objectives: Student can state Coulomb's law for the force between two point charges and write it with the constant 1/(4 pi epsilon0)
Student can write Coulomb's law in vector form and identify that F12 = -F21
Student can compare the electric force with the gravitational force between an electron and a proton
Student can define the SI unit of charge using Coulomb's law
visualIdeas: two point charges with force arrows along the line joining them
graph of force falling as 1/r^2

topics.title: Forces between Multiple Charges
objectives: Student can state the superposition principle for electrostatic forces
Student can find the net force on one charge due to several charges by adding the individual Coulomb forces as vectors
visualIdeas: three charges at the corners of a triangle with vector addition of forces

topics.title: Electric Field
objectives: Student can define electric field as force per unit positive test charge and write the field of a point charge
Student can find the electric field at a point due to a system of charges using superposition
Student can explain why the field is a physical quantity in its own right, not just a calculating device, for time-dependent situations
visualIdeas: radial field vectors around a positive and a negative point charge
field vectors from two charges added at a point

topics.title: Electric Field Lines
objectives: Student can describe field lines as curves whose tangent gives the field direction and whose density gives its strength
Student can state the properties of field lines: they start on positive and end on negative charges, do not cross and do not form closed loops in electrostatics
Student can sketch field lines for a single charge, a dipole and two equal positive charges
visualIdeas: field line patterns for +q, -q, a dipole and two like charges

topics.title: Electric Flux
objectives: Student can define electric flux through a small area as E . dS and relate it to the number of field lines crossing the area
Student can explain how the flux depends on the angle between the field and the area vector
Student can state the SI unit of electric flux
visualIdeas: field lines crossing a flat surface tilted at an angle theta
liquid flowing through a tilted ring as an analogy

topics.title: Electric Dipole
objectives: Student can define an electric dipole and its dipole moment p = q x 2a pointing from -q to +q
Student can derive the field of a dipole at a point on its axis and on its equatorial plane
Student can explain that at large distances the dipole field falls as 1/r^3
Student can distinguish polar molecules such as water from non-polar molecules such as CO2 and CH4
visualIdeas: dipole with field vectors on its axis and its equatorial line
water molecule with its permanent dipole moment

topics.title: Dipole in a Uniform External Field
objectives: Student can show that the net force on a dipole in a uniform field is zero
Student can derive the torque on a dipole, tau = p x E, and explain how it tends to align the dipole with the field
Student can explain why a dipole in a non-uniform field also feels a net force, as when a charged comb attracts bits of paper
visualIdeas: dipole in a uniform field with equal and opposite forces forming a couple

topics.title: Continuous Charge Distribution
objectives: Student can define linear, surface and volume charge densities with their units
Student can write the field of a continuous charge distribution as a sum over small charge elements
visualIdeas: charged wire, sheet and solid split into small elements dq

topics.title: Gauss's Law
objectives: Student can state Gauss's law: the total flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by epsilon0
Student can show that the flux through a sphere around a point charge is q/epsilon0, independent of the radius
Student can explain that charges outside a closed surface give zero net flux through it
Student can choose a Gaussian surface and apply Gauss's law to find enclosed charge from a given field
visualIdeas: closed Gaussian surface with charges inside and outside
field lines entering and leaving a cylinder

topics.title: Field due to an Infinitely Long Straight Uniformly Charged Wire
objectives: Student can use symmetry to argue that the field of a long charged wire is radial
Student can apply Gauss's law with a cylindrical Gaussian surface to obtain E = lambda / (2 pi epsilon0 r)
visualIdeas: charged wire inside a coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface

topics.title: Field due to a Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet
objectives: Student can use a box-shaped Gaussian surface to show that the field of an infinite charged sheet is sigma / (2 epsilon0)
Student can explain why this field does not depend on the distance from the sheet
visualIdeas: infinite sheet with a pillbox Gaussian surface through it

topics.title: Field due to a Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell
objectives: Student can show with Gauss's law that outside a charged spherical shell the field is as if all the charge were at its centre
Student can show that the field inside a uniformly charged thin shell is zero
visualIdeas: spherical shell with Gaussian spheres inside and outside
graph of E against r for a charged shell

topics.title: Electrostatic Potential
objectives: Student can explain that the Coulomb force is conservative, so work done against it is stored as potential energy
Student can define electrostatic potential at a point as the work done by an external force in bringing a unit positive charge from infinity to that point
Student can explain that only potential difference is physically significant and state the unit volt
visualIdeas: test charge pushed slowly from infinity towards a charge Q
hill analogy for potential

topics.title: Potential due to a Point Charge
objectives: Student can derive V = Q / (4 pi epsilon0 r) for a point charge
Student can compare how potential (1/r) and field (1/r^2) fall with distance
visualIdeas: graph of V and E against r for a point charge

topics.title: Potential due to an Electric Dipole
objectives: Student can derive the potential of a dipole at a general point, V = p cos theta / (4 pi epsilon0 r^2)
Student can explain why the potential is zero on the equatorial plane and why the dipole potential falls as 1/r^2
visualIdeas: dipole with a point P at angle theta from its axis

topics.title: Potential due to a System of Charges
objectives: Student can find the potential at a point due to several charges by adding their potentials algebraically
Student can state the potential outside and inside a uniformly charged spherical shell
visualIdeas: several charges around a point P with their distances marked

topics.title: Equipotential Surfaces
objectives: Student can define an equipotential surface and draw equipotentials for a point charge, a uniform field and a dipole
Student can explain why the field is always normal to an equipotential surface and no work is done moving a charge along it
Student can use E = -dV/dl to relate field to potential and state that the field points in the direction of steepest fall of potential
visualIdeas: concentric equipotential spheres around a point charge
equipotential planes perpendicular to a uniform field

topics.title: Potential Energy of a System of Charges
objectives: Student can calculate the work done in assembling two charges and write their potential energy q1 q2 / (4 pi epsilon0 r12)
Student can extend the result to three or more charges by summing over all pairs
Student can interpret the sign of the potential energy for like and unlike charges
visualIdeas: three charges being brought in from infinity one at a time

topics.title: Potential Energy in an External Field
objectives: Student can write the potential energy of a single charge q in an external potential V as qV
Student can write the potential energy of two charges in an external field including their mutual interaction term
Student can use the electron volt as a unit of energy
visualIdeas: charge placed in a region of external potential V(r)

topics.title: Potential Energy of a Dipole in an External Field
objectives: Student can calculate the work done in rotating a dipole in a uniform field
Student can write the potential energy of a dipole as U = -p . E and identify its stable and unstable orientations
visualIdeas: dipole rotated from angle theta0 to theta1 in a uniform field

topics.title: Electrostatics of Conductors
objectives: Student can state that the electrostatic field is zero inside a conductor and normal to its surface just outside
Student can explain that excess charge resides on the surface and that the potential is constant throughout a conductor
Student can relate the field at the surface to surface charge density, E = sigma / epsilon0
Student can explain electrostatic shielding: the field inside a cavity in a conductor is zero
visualIdeas: conductor with charges on the surface and field lines meeting it at right angles
cavity inside a conductor shielded from outside fields

topics.title: Dielectrics and Polarisation
objectives: Student can contrast how conductors and dielectrics respond to an external field
Student can distinguish polar and non-polar molecules and explain how each becomes polarised
Student can define polarisation and explain how a polarised slab produces surface charges that reduce the field inside it
visualIdeas: non-polar molecules stretched into dipoles by a field
polarised slab with induced surface charges

topics.title: Capacitors and Capacitance
objectives: Student can describe a capacitor as two conductors separated by an insulator
Student can define capacitance C = Q/V and state the unit farad
Student can explain why a large capacitance lets a capacitor hold a large charge at a small potential difference
visualIdeas: two plates with charges +Q and -Q and potential difference V

topics.title: The Parallel Plate Capacitor
objectives: Student can find the field between and outside the plates of a parallel plate capacitor
Student can derive C = epsilon0 A / d for a parallel plate capacitor with vacuum between the plates
visualIdeas: parallel plates with uniform field between and fringing at the edges

topics.title: Effect of Dielectric on Capacitance
objectives: Student can explain how a dielectric filling the gap reduces the field and increases capacitance
Student can define dielectric constant K as C/C0 and write C = K epsilon0 A / d
visualIdeas: capacitor with a dielectric slab and induced surface charges

topics.title: Capacitors in Series
objectives: Student can explain that capacitors in series carry the same charge
Student can derive 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2 + ... and find the equivalent capacitance of a series combination
visualIdeas: two capacitors in series across a battery

topics.title: Capacitors in Parallel
objectives: Student can explain that capacitors in parallel have the same potential difference
Student can derive C = C1 + C2 + ... and solve problems on mixed combinations
visualIdeas: two capacitors in parallel across a battery

topics.title: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
objectives: Student can derive the energy stored in a capacitor as Q^2 / 2C = CV^2 / 2 = QV / 2
Student can express the stored energy as energy density of the field, u = epsilon0 E^2 / 2
visualIdeas: graph of V against Q with the area under it shaded as stored energy

topics.title: Electric Current
objectives: Student can define electric current as the rate of flow of net charge across an area, I = dq/dt
Student can state the SI unit ampere and give typical orders of magnitude of currents
visualIdeas: charges crossing a small area normal to their flow

topics.title: Electric Currents in Conductors
objectives: Student can explain why free electrons in a conductor give no net current without an applied field
Student can describe how an electric field across a conductor produces a steady current
visualIdeas: free electrons moving randomly inside a wire

topics.title: Ohm's Law
objectives: Student can state Ohm's law, V = IR, and the unit ohm
Student can show that R = rho l / A and explain resistivity as a property of the material
Student can define current density and write Ohm's law as j = sigma E
visualIdeas: slab of conductor doubled in length and in area
V-I straight-line graph

topics.title: Drift of Electrons and the Origin of Resistivity
objectives: Student can explain drift velocity as the small average velocity electrons gain between collisions in an electric field
Student can derive I = n e A vd and the expression for resistivity in terms of relaxation time
Student can define mobility as drift velocity per unit field and state its unit
visualIdeas: zig-zag path of an electron with a small drift opposite to E

topics.title: Limitations of Ohm's Law
objectives: Student can give examples where V is not proportional to I, where the relation depends on the sign of V, or where V is not a unique function of I
Student can interpret non-linear V-I graphs such as that of a diode or GaAs
visualIdeas: non-linear V-I characteristic curves

topics.title: Resistivity of Various Materials
objectives: Student can classify materials as conductors, semiconductors and insulators by their resistivity ranges
Student can compare resistivities of metals, alloys, semiconductors and insulators from a table
visualIdeas: log-scale bar chart of resistivities

topics.title: Temperature Dependence of Resistivity
objectives: Student can write rho_T = rho_0 [1 + alpha (T - T0)] and define the temperature coefficient of resistivity
Student can explain why the resistivity of metals rises and that of semiconductors falls with temperature
Student can explain why alloys like nichrome and manganin are used for resistors
visualIdeas: resistivity against temperature graphs for copper, nichrome and a semiconductor

topics.title: Electrical Energy, Power
objectives: Student can derive the power dissipated in a resistor, P = VI = I^2 R = V^2 / R
Student can explain why power is transmitted at high voltage to reduce line losses
visualIdeas: power line from a station to a town with I^2 R loss shown as heat

topics.title: Cells, emf, Internal Resistance
objectives: Student can define emf of a cell and its internal resistance
Student can show that the terminal voltage is V = epsilon - Ir when current flows
Student can find the maximum current a cell can supply
visualIdeas: cell with electrodes, electrolyte and an external resistor R

topics.title: Cells in Series and in Parallel
objectives: Student can find the equivalent emf and internal resistance of cells connected in series
Student can find the equivalent emf and internal resistance of cells connected in parallel
visualIdeas: two cells in series and two cells in parallel with their equivalent cell

topics.title: Kirchhoff's Rules
objectives: Student can state the junction rule as conservation of charge and the loop rule as conservation of energy
Student can apply Kirchhoff's rules with sign conventions to find currents in a multi-loop network
visualIdeas: network with junction currents and loop directions marked

topics.title: Wheatstone Bridge
objectives: Student can derive the balance condition R2/R1 = R4/R3 of a Wheatstone bridge from Kirchhoff's rules
Student can use the balanced bridge to find an unknown resistance
visualIdeas: Wheatstone bridge with four resistors and a galvanometer

topics.title: Magnetic Field, Lorentz Force
objectives: Student can recall that charges produce fields and that a moving charge also produces a magnetic field B
Student can write the Lorentz force F = q[E + v x B] and explain each term
Student can explain why the magnetic force does no work and is zero for a charge at rest or moving along B
Student can define the tesla from the magnetic force on a moving charge
visualIdeas: dot and cross notation for fields out of and into the page
right-hand rule for F = q v x B

topics.title: Magnetic Force on a Current-carrying Conductor
objectives: Student can derive F = I l x B for a straight current-carrying rod in a uniform field
Student can solve problems such as the field needed to suspend a current-carrying wire
visualIdeas: straight wire in a magnetic field with force arrow upward

topics.title: Motion in a Magnetic Field
objectives: Student can show that a charge moving perpendicular to B moves in a circle and derive its radius r = mv / qB
Student can find the angular frequency and period of the circular motion
Student can describe the helical path when the velocity has a component along B and find its pitch
visualIdeas: circular orbit of a charge in a field into the page
helical path along field lines

topics.title: Magnetic Field due to a Current Element, Biot-Savart Law
objectives: Student can state the Biot-Savart law for the field dB of a current element I dl
Student can compare the Biot-Savart law with Coulomb's law
Student can relate mu0 and epsilon0 to the speed of light
visualIdeas: current element with dB at a point P perpendicular to both dl and r

topics.title: Magnetic Field on the Axis of a Circular Current Loop
objectives: Student can use the Biot-Savart law to derive the field on the axis of a circular loop
Student can find the field at the centre of a loop, B = mu0 I / 2R
Student can use the right-hand thumb rule to find the direction of the field of a loop
visualIdeas: circular loop with field lines threading through its centre

topics.title: Ampere's Circuital Law
objectives: Student can state Ampere's circuital law relating the line integral of B round a closed loop to the enclosed current
Student can use Ampere's law to find the field of a long straight wire, B = mu0 I / 2 pi r
Student can apply the right-hand rule for the direction of the field around a straight wire
visualIdeas: circular Amperian loop around a straight current

topics.title: The Solenoid
objectives: Student can describe the field pattern of a long solenoid: uniform inside and nearly zero outside
Student can apply Ampere's law to derive B = mu0 n I inside a long solenoid
visualIdeas: solenoid with field lines and a rectangular Amperian loop

topics.title: Force between Two Parallel Currents, the Ampere
objectives: Student can derive the force per unit length between two long parallel currents
Student can explain why parallel currents attract and antiparallel currents repel
Student can state the definition of the ampere from this force
visualIdeas: two parallel wires with field and force arrows

topics.title: Torque on a Rectangular Current Loop in a Uniform Magnetic Field
objectives: Student can show that the net force on a current loop in a uniform field is zero but the torque is not
Student can derive tau = m x B with magnetic moment m = NIA
Student can identify the stable and unstable equilibrium orientations of the loop
visualIdeas: rectangular loop in a field with forces on its arms forming a couple

topics.title: Circular Current Loop as a Magnetic Dipole
objectives: Student can show that the axial field of a loop at large distance has the form of a dipole field
Student can compare the magnetic dipole of a current loop with the electric dipole
visualIdeas: field lines of a current loop beside those of a bar magnet

topics.title: The Moving Coil Galvanometer
objectives: Student can explain the working of a moving coil galvanometer using the torque on a coil in a radial field
Student can define current sensitivity and voltage sensitivity of a galvanometer
Student can explain how a galvanometer is converted into an ammeter with a small shunt resistance and into a voltmeter with a large series resistance
visualIdeas: moving coil galvanometer with radial magnetic field and spring
galvanometer with a shunt and with a series resistor

topics.title: The Bar Magnet
objectives: Student can describe the pattern of iron filings around a bar magnet and draw its magnetic field lines
Student can state the properties of magnetic field lines, including that they form closed loops
Student can explain why a bar magnet behaves like an equivalent solenoid
visualIdeas: iron filings around a bar magnet and around a solenoid side by side

topics.title: The Dipole in a Uniform Magnetic Field
objectives: Student can write the restoring torque on a compass needle of moment m in a uniform field, tau = m x B, and explain why it oscillates
Student can write the magnetic potential energy U = -m . B and identify the most stable and most unstable positions
visualIdeas: compass needle oscillating about the field direction

topics.title: The Electrostatic Analog
objectives: Student can obtain the axial and equatorial fields of a bar magnet by analogy with the electric dipole
Student can compare corresponding electric and magnetic dipole quantities from a table
visualIdeas: table pairing electric dipole formulas with magnetic dipole formulas

topics.title: Magnetism and Gauss's Law
objectives: Student can state Gauss's law for magnetism: the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero
Student can explain that this means isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist
visualIdeas: closed surface around a bar magnet with as many lines entering as leaving

topics.title: Magnetisation and Magnetic Intensity
objectives: Student can define magnetisation M as net magnetic moment per unit volume
Student can define magnetic intensity H and write B = mu0 (H + M)
Student can define magnetic susceptibility and relative permeability and relate them
visualIdeas: solenoid with a material core and arrows for H, M and B

topics.title: Magnetic Properties of Materials
objectives: Student can classify materials as diamagnetic, paramagnetic or ferromagnetic by their susceptibility
Student can explain diamagnetism and the perfect diamagnetism of superconductors
Student can explain paramagnetism as the partial alignment of permanent atomic dipoles against thermal agitation
Student can explain ferromagnetism using domains, distinguish hard and soft ferromagnets, and state that a ferromagnet becomes a paramagnet at high enough temperature
visualIdeas: field lines expelled by a diamagnet and concentrated in a paramagnet
randomly oriented and aligned ferromagnetic domains

topics.title: The Experiments of Faraday and Henry
objectives: Student can describe the experiments with a magnet moved near a coil and with two coils where current is switched or changed
Student can conclude that relative motion or a changing current induces a current in a coil
visualIdeas: bar magnet pushed into a coil connected to a galvanometer
two coils with a key in the primary circuit

topics.title: Magnetic Flux
objectives: Student can define magnetic flux through a surface as B . A = BA cos theta
Student can state the SI unit of flux, the weber
visualIdeas: plane area tilted in a uniform magnetic field

topics.title: Faraday's Law of Induction
objectives: Student can state Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux
Student can calculate induced emf for a coil of N turns whose flux changes
Student can list ways of changing flux: changing B, area or orientation
visualIdeas: graph of flux against time with the slope as emf

topics.title: Lenz's Law and Conservation of Energy
objectives: Student can state Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change in flux that produces it
Student can find the direction of induced current when a magnet approaches or recedes from a coil
Student can explain Lenz's law as a consequence of conservation of energy
visualIdeas: coil facing an approaching north pole with induced current direction

topics.title: Motional Electromotive Force
objectives: Student can derive the emf epsilon = Blv induced in a rod moving across a magnetic field
Student can explain motional emf using the Lorentz force on free charges in the rod
Student can calculate the emf and current for a rod moving on rails or rotating in a field
visualIdeas: rod sliding on rails in a magnetic field with induced current

topics.title: Mutual Inductance
objectives: Student can define inductance as flux linkage per unit current
Student can derive the mutual inductance of two long co-axial solenoids
Student can write the induced emf in one coil due to changing current in another, epsilon = -M dI/dt
visualIdeas: two co-axial solenoids, one inside the other

topics.title: Self-inductance
objectives: Student can define self-inductance and derive the self-inductance of a long solenoid
Student can explain the back emf that opposes a change of current in a coil
Student can derive the energy stored in an inductor, LI^2 / 2
visualIdeas: solenoid with current rising and back emf opposing it

topics.title: AC Generator
objectives: Student can describe the parts of an ac generator and how rotating a coil in a field induces an emf

sine graph of induced emf with coil positions

visualIdeas: in-phase sine graphs of v and i for a resistor

topics.title: Representation of AC Current and Voltage by Rotating Vectors - Phasors
objectives: Student can represent an alternating voltage and current as rotating phasors

visualIdeas: phasors rotating anticlockwise with their projections as sine waves
